pairs.question: Cur ergo scriptum est: Dixit dominus ad Moysen, et non potius: Dixit angelus ad Moysen?
pairs.answer: Quia cum uerba iudicis praeco pronuntiat, non scribitur in gestis: 'Ille praeco dixit,' sed: 'Ille iudex.'
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech question framed by "'Sed,' ait aliquis," which is dropped as speech-tag/narration; the question's first word is capitalized and the trailing source quotation marks removed. The reply opens with "Quia cum uerba iudicis praeco pronuntiat..." which directly answers why scripture writes 'the Lord said' not 'the angel said' (the herald/judge analogy). Cut at the first full stop after "sed: 'Ille iudex.'"; what follows ("Sic etiam loquente propheta sancto...") is elaboration applying the analogy to prophets, so it is omitted.
